system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller's SPA positions and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary point: ignore the Seller's "pre-categorisation"

The Seller's package labels most clauses **[STANDARD]** / **FINAL**, asserts they were "settled at principal level", and asks us to review only items marked [OPEN] (there are none). We should not accept any of that:

- The labels are the Seller's own assertions, embedded in a draft from the other side. We have no instruction from the Wattlebridge deal team that any of these positions are agreed. If principals genuinely settled points, that should be confirmed by our own team, not inferred from the counterparty's draft.
- The "market context" preamble is advocacy, not evidence. Even where a range is plausibly market (e.g. caps of 10–20%), the Seller has taken the seller-friendly end of every range simultaneously and then extended the regime to places it never goes in the market (fundamental warranties, fraud, specific indemnities).
- A review that skips everything the counterparty says is "cleared" is not a review.

Every clause below is treated as open.

## 1. Limitation package (cl. 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, 8.3)

**1.1 General cap – 20% / AUD 4.8m.** At the top of the Seller's own quoted range. For a target where ~30% of revenue sits in one contract with an unresolved consent, a AUD 3.2m facility is undischarged, and there is an open data incident, the warranty package is doing real work. Push for a higher cap (I would open at 50–100% of price for general warranties and settle in the 30–50% range), or at minimum 20% coupled with a separate, uncapped-or-price-capped regime for the specific indemnities below and a meaningful retention/escrow.

**1.2 Thresholds.** De minimis of AUD 25,000 and a basket of AUD 250,000 (~1.04% of price) are within range, but the basket is drafted as a **deductible** ("only the excess above the basket is recoverable"). Push for a **tipping basket** (first-dollar recovery once the threshold is passed). Also confirm that claims arising from the same or related facts aggregate for de minimis purposes, and that the thresholds do not apply to specific indemnities, tax, title or fundamental claims.

**1.3 Time limits.** 18 months for general warranties is at the long end of the Seller's quoted range, but one phrase is the real problem: *"any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."* Combined with 1.4 and 1.5 below, this drags tax (should be 7 years, aligned with ATO amendment periods), fundamental/title (should be unlimited or 6–7 years), and specific indemnities (should be unlimited or 6 years) into an 18-month window. Reverse the default: limitations apply only where expressly stated.

**1.4 Fundamental / title warranties under the general regime.** This is **not market under any description** and should be rejected outright. Capacity, authority and title to the shares must be capped at 100% of price (at minimum), with no basket/de minimis, and a long or unlimited claim period. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept recovery of only 20% of price if the Seller does not actually own what it is selling.

**1.5 "All Claims of any nature" (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).** As drafted, the caps, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions would also apply to fraud, wilful concealment, specific indemnities, the tax indemnity, leakage claims and the Seller's covenants (e.g. restraint, pre-Completion conduct). Carve out: fraud/wilful misconduct/dishonesty; fundamental warranties; tax; specific indemnities; leakage/price adjustment; breach of covenant; and, if we accept exclusive remedy, confirm it does not exclude statutory remedies that cannot be contracted out of (misleading or deceptive conduct under the ACL is the obvious one; NSW courts treat purported exclusions sceptically).

**1.6 Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3).** The most damaging clause in the package. It bars any claim for a matter "of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter *discoverable* from the data room or public records." Problems:
- Constructive knowledge ("discoverable") effectively converts the entire data room and all public registers into a disclosure against every warranty, without any fairness test.
- Advisers' knowledge is imputed to us.
- It interacts with Schedule 7 general disclosure (see §2) to leave the warranties largely meaningless.

Position: delete. If the Seller insists on something, limit it to actual knowledge of named Buyer deal-team individuals, derived from matters *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter, and expressly state that due diligence does not reduce warranty protection.

## 2. Disclosure framework (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter)

- **General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records"** (DL 1.1–1.2) is not acceptable. Require specific disclosure against identified warranties, with a "fair disclosure" standard; limit general disclosure to a short closed list (e.g. ASIC and PPSR searches against the Company as at a stated date, which we have run ourselves).
- **Data room cut-off of 5.00pm 22 September 2026.** Today is 4 November 2026. The disclosure is six weeks stale and is silent on everything since. Require a bring-down of disclosure at signing and at Completion, with any new disclosure between signing and Completion *not* qualifying warranties (Buyer right to terminate or claim instead).
- **DL 1.4 (no admissions of anything, including that any consent or payment is required)** is fine as boilerplate but confirms the Seller is not standing behind any of the characterisations in the letter. That means we must treat every item in DL 2–10 as flagging a risk, not disclosing an answer. Note also that paragraph 1.3 is missing from the letter – ask what it was.
- **DL 11 (reservation)** explicitly tells us the Buyer must form its own view. Taken together with 1.4, the Seller is disclosing *problems* while making no representation that any of them is resolved.

## 3. Specific matters – where the SPA positions do not match the Seller's own disclosure

The striking feature of the package is that the "Seller Update" characterises items as closed while the Disclosure Letter, line by line, confirms they are not.

**3.1 Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).** SPA says consent is "addressed" and satisfied on delivery of written consent; DL 2 says no final consent and no evidence the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Push for: a proper Condition Precedent requiring Bluefen's unconditional written consent *and* satisfaction (or waiver) of the 11.3 conditions, in a form approved by the Buyer; not waivable by the Seller; Seller obligation to use **best** (not reasonable) endeavours; a long-stop date; and, if the consent is in any way conditional, a price adjustment or earn-out mechanism given revenue concentration. Consider whether a Bluefen-related revenue warranty or MAC trigger is warranted.

**3.2 Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m).** SPA proposes the release "following Completion". This is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal and with an uncapped deal risk: we would be acquiring a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt, an unexercised change-of-control trigger (cl. 8.1), and registered security, relying on the Seller to sort it out afterwards. Push for: repayment out of the purchase price at Completion via the funds flow; executed deed of release and discharge, PPSR discharge and any ASIC release delivered at Completion as a Completion deliverable; written Riverlark waiver of the cl. 8.1 change-of-control; and the AUD 3.2m plus break costs treated as Debt in the price adjustment.

**3.3 Ironquay IP (SOW3, AUD 180,000 open).** The Seller says the existing indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" is adequate. Our concern is not the AUD 180k – it is that under DD-004 cl. 7.3 **the SOW3 Project Materials have not transferred** to the Company because the fee is unpaid, and there is no confirmatory assignment. For a SaaS business, unowned development output is a core IP title gap. Push for: payment of the SOW3 fee and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay delivered *at or before Completion* (as a CP or Completion deliverable), an IP ownership warranty that is not qualified by general disclosure, and a specific indemnity covering any loss from the Company not owning or being unable to use any Ironquay deliverables – not limited to the fee amount, and outside the general cap and basket.

**3.4 Closing bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000).** The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" but has not put them in the funds flow. They are conditional on Completion and continued employment, i.e. they crystallise as liabilities of *the Company* at Completion. Push for: the AUD 420k **plus employer on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, any leave accruals)** treated as Debt / a Transaction Expense in the completion accounts or deducted from price; itemised in the funds flow; and a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Ask for the bonus letters and confirm who the payer is.

**3.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records).** The Seller's SPA note calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material"; DL 6 confirms it does not know whether the file was accessed, the scope, or whether OAIC/individual notification is required under the NDB scheme. That is not a disclosed-and-closed matter; it is an open regulatory exposure of unknown size. Push for: completion of the investigation and provision of the report before signing; a privacy/data warranty not qualified by DD-006 beyond the specific facts disclosed; a specific indemnity for all costs, notification costs, regulatory penalties and third-party claims arising from the incident, outside the cap and basket, with a long claim period; and confirmation of cyber insurance coverage and notification to insurers. Also note the increased penalty regime under the Privacy Act amendments.

**3.6 Supplier renewals (DD-008/DD-011, 3 × AUD 110,000).** "Ordinary-course operating costs" is the Seller's label; DL 8 says the letter does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Three identical AUD 110k renewals from related suppliers, which we are told to "read together", looks like a possible split of a single commitment and should be investigated for timing and whether they fall before or after the locked-box/Completion date. If they are committed pre-Completion, they should be reflected in working capital or treated as Debt-like items. Request the contracts.

**3.7 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** Both are drafted as "the document does not say consent is required". We should read the clauses ourselves rather than accept the negative framing. For the lease, confirm whether the "notification" has any consequence (e.g. right to re-rate, landlord step-in) and have the notice served as a Completion deliverable. For Mossvale, confirm that the "restriction on assignment" has no change-of-control limb and that a share sale does not trigger it; obtain a comfort letter if the contract is material.

**3.8 Title (DD-012).** The share register is the Seller's document and is prima facie evidence only. DL 10 pointedly says the Buyer has not completed its own verification. Before signing: run current ASIC company extract and PPSR searches against the Company and against the Seller (for security over the shares), check the register against the ASIC member records, confirm no options, convertible instruments or shareholder agreements, and check the Riverlark security package for a share mortgage. Title must be a fundamental warranty on the terms in §1.4.

**3.9 Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime".** No. Tax should sit under a separate tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, capped at price, 7-year period, no basket). IP should be a full warranty set given this is an analytics SaaS business, with the Ironquay carve-out as a specific indemnity.

## 4. Security for claims

Given the number of open items, an 18-month window and a counterparty that is a venture vehicle (Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd – we should check its substance and whether it will have assets post-sale), we should require a **retention/escrow** (e.g. 10–15% of price for 18–24 months, with a longer tail for the specific indemnities) or a parent/fund guarantee. W&I insurance is an option, but note insurers will exclude known matters (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006), so those need contractual indemnities regardless.

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Recommended position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "[STANDARD]/FINAL" labelling, efficiency note | Disregard; confirm internally what, if anything, principals actually agreed; review all clauses |
| 2 | General cap 20% | Open at 50–100%; settle 30–50%, plus escrow |
| 3 | Basket | Tipping, not deductible; related claims aggregate; no thresholds for fundamental/tax/indemnities |
| 4 | Time limits / "applies to all Claims" default | Reverse default; general 18–24 months; tax 7 years; fundamental/title unlimited or 7 years; indemnities 6 years+ |
| 5 | Fundamental/title warranties within general cap | Reject; cap at 100% of price, no basket, long period |
| 6 | Limitations/exclusive remedy on "all Claims" | Carve out fraud, fundamentals, tax, indemnities, leakage, covenants, non-excludable statutory rights |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge cl. 8.3 | Delete; at most actual knowledge of named individuals from fairly disclosed matters |
| 8 | General disclosure of data room/public records | Reject; specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties only |
| 9 | Disclosure cut-off 22 Sept 2026 | Bring-down at signing and Completion; new matters do not qualify warranties |
| 10 | Bluefen | Non-waivable CP: unconditional consent + 11.3 conditions satisfied; best endeavours; consider price protection |
| 11 | Riverlark | Repay at Completion from price; discharge, PPSR release and CoC waiver as Completion deliverables; treat as Debt |
| 12 | Ironquay | SOW3 paid and confirmatory IP assignment delivered pre-Completion; uncapped specific IP indemnity |
| 13 | Closing bonuses | AUD 420k + on-costs as Debt/Transaction Expense in funds flow; indemnity for shortfall |
| 14 | DD-006 privacy incident | Finish investigation pre-signing; specific indemnity outside cap/basket; insurance confirmation |
| 15 | Sandbar renewals | Obtain contracts; test "ordinary course"; adjust via completion accounts if committed |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Review clauses directly; serve notice / obtain comfort as Completion deliverables |
| 17 | Title | Independent ASIC/PPSR verification; check for share security and dilutive instruments |
| 18 | Tax / IP | Separate tax indemnity; full IP warranty set |
| 19 | Recourse | Escrow/retention or guarantee; consider W&I for unknown matters only |

**Overall assessment:** the Seller Update presents the deal as substantially closed, but the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms that the four largest risk items (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay IP transfer, the DD-006 incident) are all unresolved, and the liability package is drafted so that the Buyer would have little practical recourse on any of them. The combination of general data-room disclosure, constructive-knowledge exclusion, deductible basket, 20% cap and the extension of that cap to fundamental and indemnity claims is the core problem and should be the focus of the mark-up, alongside converting each open item into a CP, Completion deliverable or ring-fenced indemnity.

If useful, I can prepare a clause-by-clause mark-up of the Seller's positions or a draft issues list for the next principal-level call.
=== END ADVICE ===
